newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open higher but tight range seen.
newsitem.headline: German shares open higher but tight range seen.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index opened around one percent higher on Monday, reflecting the strong gain made in Friday's post-bourse trade after U.S. jobs data seen as easing immediate prospects for a U.S. rate hike.
The DAX which tracks Germany's leading 30 shares gained 24.98 points, or 0.99 percent, to 2,541.98 in early trade, supported by steady dollar-mark trading and fractionally stronger German bunds.

But dealers said the move upwards, rather than reflecting any real optimism, was largely the result of so-called "short-covering", where market players needed to buy securities in the market to complete earlier "sell" positions.
"People are still a bit sceptical about the future direction," one dealer said, adding that he saw the DAX index trading in a tight range of between 2,540 and 2,550 points.
The IBIS all-day electronic trade index, which had already reflected gains on Friday, traded a small 2.78 points up at 2,545.22, while the September DAX future gained 1.5 points at 2,548.5.

Shares in car-maker Volkswagen traded 6.75 marks higher at 555 marks after a weekend German press report that it planned to boost its meagre return on sales ration by tenfold by the end of the decade.
VW chief Ferdinand Piech said he saw U.S.-based Chrysler -- with a return on sales of 6.6 percent compared to VW's 0.6 percent -- as a model for the company.
Commercial bank Deutsche Bank, still suffering image problems after last week's temporary suspension of dealing in three of its British-based funds, traded 27 pfennigs weaker at 71.77 marks.
